clue.text: "Ocean" corrected to "sea" here

indicators.note: a word that is corrected is altered, so its letters are put into a new order

parts.note: the Ross Sea is a sea off Antarctica, so sea can stand for Ross

explanation.surface: A proof-reader's note: the word 'ocean' should be changed to 'sea' at this point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'corrected' signals the anagram. Sea gives Ross via the Ross Sea off Antarctica. The definition 'here' is self-referential: this clue sits in the grid's first across slot.
explanation.definitionFit: The clue itself is the puzzle's first across entry, so 'here' points to its own position.

clue.text: See 21
Absorb outside capital (less a pound) and remove gently

indicators.note: the eating word is placed around the other piece, wrapping outside it

parts.note: to absorb food is to eat it

indicators.note: less means minus, so the pound letter is subtracted from the city

parts.note: Seoul is the capital of South Korea
L, from Latin libra, is the abbreviation for a pound

explanation.surface: Instructions for a delicate manoeuvre involving absorbing a city and coaxing something free.
explanation.walkthrough: 'less' drops the pound sign from the South Korean capital, and 'outside' wraps the eating word round what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: To ease something out is a phrasal verb for extracting it slowly and carefully.

clue.text: Rail company has service to take in food

parts.note: RN, the Royal Navy, is one of the armed services

indicators.note: the take letter is placed in the middle of the food word

parts.note: cake is a kind of food
R stands for Latin recipe, meaning take, as written on old prescriptions

explanation.surface: A railway firm offers a catering service so passengers can get something to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rail' is not a railway but a marsh bird, of which the corncrake is one.
explanation.definitionFit: The corncrake is a species of bird in the rail family, so it is an example of a rail.

clue.text: See 24
Multifaceted area — see the last one encased in shutters

indicators.note: the middle pieces are enclosed within the shutters word, as if in a case

parts.note: seals are things that shut something tight
V stands for Latin vide, meaning see
the end is the last part of something
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A description of a district: take a look at the final building, boarded up behind shutters.
explanation.walkthrough: Seven Dials is a London junction where seven streets meet at a pillar bearing sundials, hence 'multifaceted'.
explanation.definitionFit: The London district is named after a column carrying many sundial faces, so it is an area with many faces.

clue.text: See 3
Take charge of breeding ground where there's a tie?

parts.note: to collar someone is to seize or take control of them
a stud is a farm where horses are bred

explanation.surface: Seizing control of a breeding farm ends in a dead heat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tie' suggests a draw in a contest, but it is the necktie, which sits at the collar fastening.
explanation.definitionFit: A collar stud fastens a detachable shirt collar, the place a necktie is worn.

clue.text: Fungus from an island part of Italy

parts.note: the Isle of Man is an island in the Irish Sea

indicators.note: only a part of the country's name is used, its final letters dropped

parts.note: the country's name is written in full before being cut

explanation.surface: A mushroom coming from a particular island region of Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: Amanita is a genus of mushrooms including the fly agaric and death cap.

clue.text: Coming out of Greece with men at sea

indicators.note: being at sea means confused or all over the place, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Leaving Greece in the company of sailors on the water.
explanation.definitionFit: Emergence is the act of coming out into view, a noun matching the gerund.

clue.text: Goldsmith's work for house inside worth being given advantage

parts.note: a desert is what one merits, as in getting one's just deserts

indicators.note: the house word is put within the advantage word

parts.note: an edge is an advantage over a rival
a villa is a kind of house

explanation.surface: A goldsmith works on a valuable house given an extra feature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Goldsmith' is Oliver Goldsmith, the poet, not a metalworker.
explanation.definitionFit: The Deserted Village is a 1770 poem by Oliver Goldsmith.

clue.text: Bird's eggs found on sideboard?

parts.note: a rook is a black bird of the crow family
spawn is the mass of eggs laid by fish or frogs

explanation.surface: Some bird's eggs turn up on a dining-room cabinet.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces split differently from the answer: the S of the possessive moves into the eggs. 'sideboard' is read as side of the board: in chess this pawn starts on an outermost file.
explanation.definitionFit: In chess the pawn in front of each rook stands on the edge file of the board.

clue.text: Soon Old English will be attractive

parts.note: something that will soon be old is ageing

explanation.surface: Before long, Old English will become appealing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old English' looks like a single phrase, but it splits: English ageing will be old soon.
explanation.definitionFit: Engaging means charming, a synonym for attractive in manner.

clue.text: Former party leader game to cross the line

parts.note: Michael Foot led the British Labour Party from 1980 to 1983
bridge is a card game

explanation.surface: An ex-leader of a political party plays a game to cross the floor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the line' is a railway line, which a footbridge carries walkers over.
explanation.definitionFit: A footbridge is built to let pedestrians get over a railway or road.

clue.text: Spin with the right look, you might say

indicators.note: signals that the phrase is to be heard spoken, not read

parts.note: proper means right and a gander is a look

explanation.surface: Political spin delivered with exactly the right appearance.
explanation.definitionFit: Spin is the presentation of information with a bias, the same idea as biased promotional messaging.

clue.text: Fragrant medley of Roman Catholicism, say?

indicators.note: the word is to be spoken, as if quoted out loud

parts.note: popery is an old hostile term for Roman Catholicism

explanation.surface: A sweet-smelling mixture associated with the Catholic Church, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: The French-derived answer is pronounced roughly 'po-poo-ree', close to 'popery'.
explanation.definitionFit: A potpourri is a bowl of mixed dried petals and spices kept for its scent.

clue.text: Mate on a board that can be accepted

parts.note: mate and pal both mean a friend
a table is a board, as in board and lodging

explanation.surface: A friend climbs on a board that is deemed acceptable.
explanation.definitionFit: Palatable means agreeable or acceptable, extended from food pleasant to taste.

clue.text: See 10
See 23
Depress duck

definitions.meaning: to depress someone is to make them feel low
to duck is to drop down quickly out of sight

explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both to make someone miserable and to crouch low to avoid something.

clue.text: Influence of the upper class, dead, to breed abundantly

parts.note: pull is influence, as in having pull with someone
U is short for upper class, as in Nancy Mitford's U and non-U
late means dead, as in the late king

explanation.surface: The power of the toffs, long gone, used to multiply prolifically.
explanation.definitionFit: To pullulate is to multiply rapidly or teem, as with offspring.

clue.text: A boy having a row with a lamp

parts.note: lad means boy
a din is a noisy row

explanation.surface: A boy is quarrelling with someone about a lamp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' wants to be a line, but it rhymes with cow here: a noisy din.
explanation.definitionFit: The folk-tale hero is famous for his magic lamp and its genie.

clue.text: Teaching worked out during most of play

indicators.note: one piece occurs during the other, so it sits inside it
only most of the play word is used, losing its last letters

parts.note: a tragedy is a kind of play

indicators.note: worked means manipulated, signalling that the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A tutor's lesson was figured out in the middle of the drama.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worked' signals the anagram of 'out'; 'most of' trims the drama word; 'during' sets one inside the other. Tutoring and tutorial fit the length too, but neither fits this wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Tutorage is the work or office of a tutor, so it means teaching.

clue.text: Regulation of height is a lot to ask

parts.note: tall means of great height
an order is a regulation or rule

explanation.surface: Rules about how high things may be are quite a demand.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall order is an idiom for a demanding request, something hard to fulfil.

clue.text: Left some silver, which is generous

indicators.note: only some of the silver word is used, its tail dropped

parts.note: argent is heraldic silver

explanation.surface: Someone left a bit of silver in a will, which was kind.
explanation.definitionFit: Large in an old sense means liberal or generous, as in large-hearted.

clue.text: Sailor hid by little space traveller

indicators.note: the sailor is hidden by the other word, enclosed within it

parts.note: slight means small or little
tar is a traditional word for a sailor

explanation.surface: A seaman is concealed by a small astronaut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'space traveller' suggests an astronaut, but it is light from stars crossing space.
explanation.definitionFit: Light from distant stars travels across space to reach Earth.

clue.text: Barbarian to run all but the north country the morning after?

parts.note: the Huns were barbarian invaders of Europe

indicators.note: all but means everything except the named letter, so it is dropped

parts.note: to run a country is to govern it

explanation.surface: A barbarian rules everywhere bar the north of the land the day after.
explanation.walkthrough: 'country the morning after' puns on Hungary, as if the land's name were said after a night out.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling ill after heavy drinking is the classic state of the morning after.

clue.text: No hat? Odd — possible mistake about that to be melodramatic

indicators.note: the mistake word goes about, surrounding, the anagram

parts.note: a blunder is a mistake

indicators.note: possible suggests one of several arrangements, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Not wearing a hat? Strange; that could be an error worth making a scene about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possible' signals the anagram of the eight letters in 'No hat Odd', and 'about' wraps the error word round them; 'that' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Blood-and-thunder describes sensational, violently dramatic entertainment.

clue.text: Bond boy, one caught by raptor

indicators.note: the one is caught and held inside the bird

parts.note: an erne is a sea eagle, a bird of prey
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A young lad in a spy story is snatched by a bird of prey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bond' suggests James Bond, but it is Premium Bonds, whose prize-drawing machine is called ERNIE.
explanation.definitionFit: ERNIE is the random number machine that picks Premium Bond winners, its name a boy's name.

clue.text: Cargo near wrecking through high-handedness

indicators.note: wrecking breaks something up, so the letters are scattered and reformed

explanation.surface: A ship's cargo was lost near the rocks through overbearing behaviour.
explanation.definitionFit: Arrogance is overbearing pride, behaviour that is high-handed toward others.
